name: Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International Airport
before:
Kolkata's airport and the main aviation hub for eastern and north eastern India, at Dum Dum about 16 km from Dalhousie Square. It handled around 22 million passengers in the year to March 2025, sixth busiest in the country.

Its real value is the reach into places other Indian airports do not serve well. This is a major centre for flights into north east India, Bangladesh and Bhutan, as well as Southeast Asia and the Gulf cities of Dubai, Doha and Abu Dhabi.

Capacity has just improved. The primary runway handles about 35 flights an hour and the secondary, normally used as a taxiway, another 15. Work through 2025 lifted the airport's operating capacity from 35 to 45 flights an hour by September.

The integrated Terminal 2 covers 233,000 square metres.

Opened in 1924, this is one of the oldest airports in India. The code CCU comes from Calcutta, the city's name until 2001, and the airport was renamed in 1995 after Subhas Chandra Bose.
after:
Kolkata's airport, at Dum Dum about 16 km from Dalhousie Square, and the busiest in eastern and north eastern India. It handled about 21.1 million passengers in the year to March 2026, sixth busiest in the country.

International flights serve Bangladesh and Bhutan as well as Dubai.

The airport is named after Subhas Chandra Bose.

No source from the last 12 months could be read for the rest: Qatar Airways, Etihad and IndiGo reset the connection, Thai Airways' page loads only its home page, Khaleej Times' report of Etihad's Abu Dhabi to Kolkata flights dates from 2023, and CAPA's note of IndiGo's Kolkata to Siem Reap plan (2 October 2025) is a headline only. 'Major centre' rests on Wikipedia.
Rests on the runway claims below, which could not be confirmed.

claims.wasBefore: The primary runway handles about 35 flights an hour and the secondary, normally used as a taxiway, another 15.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The Times of India, which it cites for the runway work, is blocked by the egress policy.

claims.claim: operating capacity raised from 35 to 45 flights an hour by September 2025
claims.wasBefore: Work through 2025 lifted the airport's operating capacity from 35 to 45 flights an hour by September.

claims.wasBefore: The integrated Terminal 2 covers 233,000 square metres.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, and the one official figure found differs: the 2008 cabinet approval (PIB) planned a building of 1,80,000 square metres. anna.aero's 2013 opening report could not be reached.

claims.wasBefore: Opened in 1924, this is one of the oldest airports in India.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The airport's own site (nscbiairport.com) timed out, and its old history pages that Wikipedia cites survive only in the web archive, which the network policy blocks.

claims.wasBefore: The code CCU comes from Calcutta, the city's name until 2001
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; Britannica answered with a Cloudflare check and was not retried.
